questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving binary trees and traversals.
questions.stem: For this problem, a complete two-valued tree structure has height 3. What is the maximum number of nodes it can contain?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "counts only the deepest level" gives 8, not 15.
Wrong belief "omits the final subtraction of one" gives 16, not 15.
Wrong belief "adds one instead of subtracting" gives 17, not 15.

questions.explanation: A complete binary tree of height 3 has all levels filled, giving 2 to the power (3+1) minus 1 nodes, namely 15.
questions.hint: Sum the geometric series of level sizes.
